title: How the Coalition for Secure AI Prepares Defenders

segments.text: Good afternoon everyone. Glad to see
everyone here both in person and online.
My name is Jason Garmin. I am a
principal security solutions architect
at Amazon Web Services and today I am
asking for your help. I'm here to talk
to you briefly about the Coalition for
Secure AI or COSI. This is a group of
over 45 different organizations that
have come together to help defenders of
systems use AI effectively and defend
against AI powered threats, give them
the resources and tools that they need
to do so. And I'm here to ask for your
help and how you can contribute into
this project as well.
So, as I mentioned before, COSI consists
of about 45 plus different
organizations,
including my friend Chris over here from
Zened, who's one of our newest members
who's joined just recently. So, we
include some of the biggest hyperscalers
of the world, including Microsoft,
Amazon, Google, we have Nvidia as a
partner as well. And we have security
and AI experts from those companies and
all around the globe that are helping to
develop best practices for secure AI
deployment, AI security research and so
on.
Now, I talked to a lot of customers that
range in size from small startups all
the way into the biggest Fortune 500
companies that operate around the globe.
But they all share the same concerns no
matter what size that they operate at.
We are entering into a era, we are in
the era where there is a lot of
confusion and a lot of just not a lot of
understanding of what the best practices
are to address these new threats.
Heck, at this point we don't even have
the terms to describe what some of these
concerns are. We heard in the keynote
just this morning about how we should
use this new term and how to describe
integrity in our AI systems. How do we
think about responsible AI and
disambiguate between security and
integrity? What do those things even
mean? How do we address that? How do we
think about model security? How do we
think about signing and providence of
these AI models? And that's where COSI
comes into play.
The way that we've described or that we
divied up this uh effort is into four
different work streams. The first is our
supply chain security for AI systems.
And what we're looking to do here is to
understand how we can take existing
supply chain uh mechanisms and apply
them into new AI systems as well. So we
have a couple of special interest groups
that have come out of this as well as a
publication on AI model signing that's
available now from the COSAI website.
The second work stream is how we can
prepare defenders for a changing
landscape. So obviously these new AI
systems present new threats and
opportunities for defenders and this
workstream aims to help them arm them
with best practices around how to do
zero trust with AI systems, how to
understand to do uh you know like uh
incident response when there is an
incident with an AI system and so forth
and so on. The third work stream is on
AI security and risk governance. So
thinking about things like an AI
taxonomy as we mentioned before we have
the COSI risk map which is based on the
Google safe framework they've
contributed that into COSI and we also
have contributions from Cisco for
codeguard which is their mechanism for
doing secure code development using
agentic systems
and then finally our newest fourth
workstream is how to do secure design
patterns for agentic systems.
So again we have some exa some uh some
publications here as well on how to do
uh agentic security or to do security
for agentic systems some best practices
around that.
Now COI does not live in a vacuum. Our
idea here is we want to work with the
entire AI security ecosystem. We don't
want to reinvent the wheel. So therefore
we work with a lot of some you know a
lot of these different uh security um
you know uh uh open- source providers
that you've heard of before such as OASP
and ML Commons. We work with the cloud
security alliance and in fact a lot of
the contributors that sit on COI also
work with these other uh these other
organizations as well and we work with
organizations you may not expect such as
open SSF for example.
The idea here is we want to take the
best practices from all of the other
parts of cyber security and apply them
to AI.
Remember AI doesn't mean we have to
reinvent everything. We already have 20
plus years of experience doing things
like signing provenence uh documents for
bill of materials. Let's use that and
just adapt it to this new AI
methodology.
So finally I'll leave you with this how
you can get involved. You can always
monitor observe we have uh everything is
on GitHub we have an open slack channel
and please consider joining COSI scan
the QR code and thank you so much I look
forward to meeting you.
